ac:rich-text-body.p: Understand D-POAF® in 15 minutes. Implement it in your first Wave today.

The Core Problem: 92% of developers now use AI coding tools daily (GitHub Octoverse, 2024). But when something goes wrong in production, teams often cannot answer: who decided this? Which prompt produced it? Was it aligned with the original business requirement?

p: D-POAF® (Decentralized Proof-Oriented AI Framework) is an open-source governance framework designed to make AI-enabled software delivery structured, traceable, and provable, by design, not as an afterthought.

D-POAF does not replace your existing tools (Git, Jira, CI/CD). It adds a governance layer on top: a structured unit of work called a Wave that captures AI context, human decisions, and structured evidence across every phase of delivery.

ul.li: Proof over assumption. No AI contribution without traceability.
Roles over ad-hoc. Accountability is a structural property of delivery, not a documentation exercise.
Living Governance. Governance evolves with the team, no single authority owns the rules.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Published: D-POAF® was published in 2025 on CERN's Zenodo infrastructure with citable DOIs. It predates the January 2026 wave of AI Software Engineering standards, one of the first governance frameworks specifically designed for AI-native software delivery.

p: Everything in D-POAF® is organized around a Wave: a governed container for a unit of AI-enabled work. Think of a Wave as a smart sprint, one that not only tracks what was done, but why it was done, how the AI contributed, and what proof exists that it worked.
A Wave is not a ticket, not a sprint, and not a project. It is a self-contained unit of work that structures AI contributions across six dimensions.

tr.th: What it governs inside the Wave

tr.td: Defines objectives, boundaries, and the business requirement chain for the Wave.
Records early AI experiments, tool evaluations, and prompt context decisions before implementation.
Maintains the register of prompts, model versions, context snapshots, and AI reasoning.
Tracks implementation activity including AI-generated contributions and human decisions.
Produces structured evidence: Proof of Delivery (PoD), Proof of Value (PoV), Proof of Reliability (PoR).
Documents the auditable chain from business requirement to deployed outcome.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Practical tip: You do not need to fill all 6 dimensions perfectly on your first Wave. Start with Scope, AI Context, and Proofs. Add the others as your team gets comfortable with the framework.

h2: 3. The 5 Documents of the Starter Kit

tr.td: This page. Concepts, roles, lifecycle, implementation.

At the start of every Wave.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Minimum viable start: You can run your first Wave with just Dynamic Laws + Wave Scope + Proof Record. Add the PromptRegister from your first prompt onwards. The guide is your reference — you do not need to re-read it for every Wave.

tr.td: Single accountable owner of the Wave. Signs off on Proof Record.
Prepares context, retrieves data, structures requirements for prompts.
Drafts and refines Prompt Actions. Manages the PromptRegister.
Automated generator. Operates under explicit human boundaries.
Security, compliance, and reliability guardrails. Audit role.
Contributors who participate in Dynamic Laws and feedback loops.

h2: 5. The Proof Model — PoD / PoV / PoR
p: Every Wave produces three families of evidence:

tr.td: The deliverable exists and works as specified. (artifacts, tests, validations)
The deliverable achieved the promised business outcome. (metrics, KPIs)
The deliverable is compliant, secure, and operationally reliable. (audits, monitoring, anomalies)

ol.li: Read — agree which laws to adopt with your team.
Open your first page (create one from the Wave Scope template).
At Wave close, create a page (from the Proof Record template).
